sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Marks the file as browser-only and loads the links, page path tool, state tools, the mode toggle, and mode.
sections.why: The bar needs each of these parts.

sections.name: navItems
sections.title: Navigation items
sections.what: Lists each link with its plain label, technical label, and optional path used to highlight the current page.
sections.why: Keeps the link list in one place for both menus.
sections.watch_out: Changing this list changes both the desktop and mobile menus.

sections.name: SiteNav (part 1)
sections.title: Scroll state and desktop links
sections.what: Adds a background once the page scrolls more than 24 pixels, closes the mobile menu on page change, and draws the site name and desktop links with the current page highlighted.
sections.why: A plain background over the top of the page becomes solid after scrolling for readability.
sections.watch_out: The scroll listener is removed on unmount to avoid leaks.

sections.name: SiteNav (part 2)
sections.title: Mobile controls and menu
sections.what: Shows the mode toggle and menu button on narrow screens, and the full link list when the menu is open.
sections.why: Narrow screens need a menu instead of a row of links.
sections.watch_out: The mobile list reuses the same items, so both menus stay in step.

summary: The top navigation bar: site name, menu links, a mode toggle, and a mobile menu.
purpose: Lets visitors move around the site from any page.
why: A shared bar keeps navigation the same on every page.
how: Tracks scrolling to add a background, tracks the mobile menu state, and closes the mobile menu on each page change. Shows links on wide screens and a menu button on narrow ones.
inputs: The current page path, the mode, and the list of nav items.
outputs: A fixed header with links, a mode toggle, and a mobile list.
risks: The nav item list is exported, so changing it changes both the desktop and mobile menus.
debug: If a link is not highlighted, check its match value against the page path. If the background does not change on scroll, check the scroll listener. If the mobile menu stays open, check the page change handling.
